title: How Cal AI used a small army of paid influencers to reach $30M in revenue in two years
summary: Zach Yadegari explains at TechCrunch Disrupt how Cal AI grew virally by recruiting and paying many small influencers. He spotted early signal when one post drove about a thousand users in two days, then scaled by negotiating performance-based payouts with creators who have tight communities.

principles.text: When a single influencer post drives measurable signups, treat it as proof the channel works and scale it immediately.
principles.quote: From there, we figured out, okay, this can actually work for us, and so we started recruiting influencers as fast as we could — paying as many people as possible to start posting for us

principles.text: Influencer marketing can be a predictable, near-linear formula: each post reaches a quantifiable audience that converts at a steady rate.
principles.quote: What we saw was that it was a clear formula. It was pretty linear, but it was extremely fast.

principles.text: Pay influencers for outcomes: set a payout tied to a target number of users and have them keep posting until they hit it.
principles.quote: You just ask them, okay, we’ll pay you this, but we need to get us at least this amount of use and keep posting until you get there.

principles.text: Many small creators are motivated by cash, so negotiate rates against reach rather than chasing only big names.
principles.quote: A lot of influencers are “broke college kids” who “just want cash,”

principles.text: Choose influencers with tight communities, since their reach is easier to quantify and convert.
